title: Technology Trends Outlook 2023
notes: 81-page report, 15 trends in five groups. Equity investment (2022, $ billion) and job-postings change (2021–22) are printed per trend and recorded in each trend's note. Adoption score (0-5) is shown only graphically and is not recorded. The 2023-v5 PDF snapshot of 2024-09-14 is truncated (1 MB); the 2025-02-01 snapshot is complete. rank = contents order; forecast entries carry their trend's rank.

entries.label: Applied AI
entries.quote: With AI capabilities, such as machine learning (ML), computer vision, and natural-language processing (NLP), companies in all industries can use data and derive insights to automate processes, add or augment capabilities, and make better decisions.
entries.subject: Applied AI
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $104 billion; job postings 2021–22: +6%.

entries.label: Industrializing machine learning
entries.quote: Industrializing machine learning (ML), commonly referred to as ML operations, or MLOps, refers to the engineering practices needed to scale and sustain ML applications in an enterprise.
entries.subject: MLOps
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $3 billion; job postings 2021–22: +23%.

entries.label: Industrializing machine learning
entries.quote: IDC predicts that 60 percent of enterprises will have implemented MLOps by 2024.
entries.subject: MLOps adoption
entries.metric: share of enterprises that have implemented MLOps
entries.note: Attributed in the text to IDC.

entries.label: Generative AI
entries.quote: Generative AI marks a tipping point for AI.
entries.subject: Generative AI
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $5 billion; job postings 2021–22: +44%. New trend in 2023.

entries.label: Generative AI
entries.quote: we anticipate significant growth across metrics in 2023.
entries.subject: Generative AI momentum
entries.note: From the 'Scoring the trend' text; metrics = interest, investment, innovation, talent as scored by the report.

entries.label: Generative AI
entries.quote: Hiring demand in 2023 will likely be significantly higher due to increased interest and investment.
entries.subject: Generative AI talent demand
entries.note: Talent-market section.

entries.label: Next-generation software development
entries.quote: Adoption may be slow due to technical challenges, the need for large-scale retraining of developers and test engineers, and other organizational hurdles.
entries.subject: Software development tooling (low-code, AI-assisted)
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $2 billion; job postings 2021–22: +29%. Opening sentence split across columns; second sentence quoted.

entries.label: Next-generation software development
entries.quote: By 2026, Gartner predicts that 80 percent of low- and no-code tool users will sit outside of traditional IT organizations.
entries.subject: Low-code/no-code users
entries.metric: share of low-/no-code tool users outside IT organizations
entries.note: Attributed in the text to Gartner.

entries.label: Trust architectures and digital identity
entries.quote: Digital-trust technologies enable organizations to manage technology and data risks, accelerate innovation, and protect assets.
entries.subject: Digital trust and digital identity
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $47 billion; job postings 2021–22: +16%.

entries.label: Web3
entries.quote: Web3 goes beyond the typical understanding of cryptocurrency investments—it more significantly refers to a future model for the internet that decentralizes authority and redistributes it to users
entries.subject: Web3
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $62 billion; job postings 2021–22: +40%.

entries.label: Advanced connectivity
entries.quote: Advanced-connectivity improvements will enhance user experiences for consumers worldwide and increase productivity in industries such as mobility, healthcare, and manufacturing.
entries.subject: Advanced connectivity
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $118 billion; job postings 2021–22: +7%.

entries.label: Immersive-reality technologies
entries.quote: Immersive-reality technologies use spatial computing to interpret physical space; simulate the addition of data, objects, and people to real-world settings; and enable interactions in virtual worlds
entries.subject: Immersive reality (AR/VR/MR)
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $16 billion; job postings 2021–22: +10%.

entries.label: Immersive-reality technologies
entries.quote: Our research suggests that the emerging metaverse could generate up to $4 trillion to $5 trillion in value across consumer and enterprise use cases by 2030.
entries.subject: Metaverse value

entries.label: Immersive-reality technologies
entries.quote: New VR headsets are also expected throughout 2023, and peripheral devices (for example, haptics and displays) continue to advance
entries.subject: VR headsets

entries.label: Cloud and edge computing
entries.quote: In the future, enterprises will leverage an infrastructure footprint that involves compute and storage at multiple location points, from on-premises to closer-to-premises (the edge) and from small regional data centers to remote hyperscale data centers.
entries.subject: Cloud and edge computing
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $84 billion; job postings 2021–22: +12%.

entries.label: Quantum technologies
entries.quote: Quantum technologies promise to take advantage of the unique properties of quantum mechanics to perform specific types of complex calculations exponentially more efficiently than classical computers
entries.subject: Quantum technologies
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $2 billion; job postings 2021–22: +12%.

entries.label: Future of mobility
entries.quote: More than a century after mass production of automobiles began, mobility has arrived at a second great inflection point: a shift toward autonomous driving, connectivity, the electrification of vehicles, and shared-mobility (ACES) technologies.
entries.subject: Mobility (autonomous, connected, electric, shared)
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $194 billion; job postings 2021–22: +15%.

entries.label: Future of mobility
entries.quote: autonomous-driving technologies are projected to create up to $400 billion in revenue by 2035.
entries.subject: Autonomous-driving revenue

entries.label: Future of mobility
entries.quote: Meanwhile, market size estimates for the micromobility and minimobility industries advanced to $440 billion and $100 billion by 2030, respectively.
entries.subject: Micromobility market
entries.note: Same sentence: minimobility $100 billion by 2030. Footnote marker removed from quote.

entries.label: Future of mobility
entries.quote: the global automotive software market is also expected to grow rapidly at a 5.5 percent CAGR from 2019 to 2030.
entries.subject: Automotive software market
entries.metric: CAGR of global automotive software market 2019–2030

entries.label: Future of bioengineering
entries.quote: Breakthroughs in biology, combined with innovations in digital technology, could help organizations respond to demands in areas as diverse as healthcare, food and agriculture, consumer products, sustainability, and energy and materials production by creating new products and services.
entries.subject: Bioengineering
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $43 billion; job postings 2021–22: –19%.

entries.label: Future of bioengineering
entries.quote: McKinsey research suggests that 400 use cases for bioengineering, almost all of which are scientifically feasible today, could have an economic impact of $2 trillion to $4 trillion per year from 2030 to 2040.
entries.subject: Bioengineering economic impact
entries.metric: annual economic impact of bioengineering use cases
entries.note: A page header ('Future of bioengineering') interrupts the sentence in the PDF text and is omitted. Range 2030-2040; target_year is the end of the range. Same figure as 2022.

entries.label: Future of bioengineering
entries.quote: Present estimates suggest that cultivated meat could provide 0.5 percent of the world’s meat supply by 2030, representing billions of pounds of meat and up to $25 billion in revenue.
entries.subject: Cultivated meat
entries.metric: share of world meat supply from cultivated meat
entries.note: Same sentence: up to $25 billion revenue.

entries.label: Future of space technologies
entries.quote: The most significant development for the space industry in the past five to ten years has been decreasing technology costs, which are making new capabilities and applications more accessible.
entries.subject: Space technologies
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $8 billion; job postings 2021–22: +16%.

entries.label: Future of space technologies
entries.quote: analysis suggests that the space market could exceed $1 trillion by 2030.
entries.subject: Space economy

entries.label: Future of space technologies
entries.quote: Several new highly anticipated launch vehicles are expected to debut in 2023 and 2024, including the SpaceX’s superheavy Starship, designed to carry larger loads; the Vulcan Centaur, from United Launch Alliance, which is designed to carry satellites into orbit; and Blue Origin’s New Glenn
entries.subject: New heavy launch vehicles
entries.note: Vehicles named: Starship, Vulcan Centaur, New Glenn.

entries.label: Electrification and renewables
entries.quote: Electrification and renewables help drive toward net-zero commitments and include solar-, wind-, and hydro-powered renewables and other renewables; nuclear energy; hydrogen; sustainable fuels; and electric-vehicle charging.
entries.subject: Electrification and renewable energy
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $288 billion; job postings 2021–22: +27%. Short profile (one page shared with trend 15); footnote: capex-related investments for 2022 totaled $578 billion.

entries.label: Climate technologies beyond electrification and renewables
entries.quote: Climate technologies include carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS); carbon removals; natural climate solutions; circular technologies; alternative proteins and agriculture; water and biodiversity solutions and adaptation; and technologies to track net-zero progress.
entries.subject: Climate technologies (CCUS, carbon removal, circularity)
entries.note: Report states (past-year context, not a forecast): equity investment 2022: $86 billion; job postings 2021–22: +8%. Short profile; footnote: capex-related investments for 2022 totaled $98 billion.
